summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of sectoral mutual funds, their risks, benefits, and taxation in India, though some tax figures are outdated.

claims.claim: Sectoral mutual funds are a category of equity funds that invest a minimum of 80% of their assets in equities and equity-related instruments of companies operating in a particular sector, as defined by SEBI.
claims.note: SEBI regulations mandate that sectoral funds invest a minimum of 80% of their total assets in equity and equity-related instruments of a single sector.

claims.claim: Sectoral funds are treated as equity-oriented mutual funds for taxation purposes, provided they invest at least 65% of their assets in Indian equities.
claims.note: Sectoral funds are classified as equity-oriented mutual funds for tax purposes because they typically invest more than the 65% equity threshold required for this classification.

claims.claim: If you redeem your units in a sectoral mutual fund within 12 months of purchase, any profit generated is considered a Short-Term Capital Gain (STCG). This STCG is taxed at a flat rate of 15% (plus applicable surcharge and cess).
claims.note: While STCG for equity-oriented mutual funds held for less than 12 months was 15% previously, recent changes (effective July 23, 2024, as per some sources) indicate it is now 20%.

claims.claim: For equity-oriented mutual funds, LTCG up to ₹1 lakh in a financial year is exempt from tax. However, LTCG exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year is taxed at a rate of 10% without indexation benefit.
claims.note: The LTCG exemption limit for equity-oriented mutual funds is ₹1.25 lakh per financial year, not ₹1 lakh. Also, LTCG exceeding this limit is taxed at 12.5%, not 10%, as per recent updates (effective July 23, 2024, or Union Budget 2024/2025).

claims.claim: If you hold your units for more than 12 months before redemption, any profit is classified as a Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG).
claims.note: For equity-oriented mutual funds, a holding period of more than 12 months qualifies for Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG).

article_title: Sectoral Mutual Funds: Risks, Returns, and Key Considerations
